nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 1$, the integer power series $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ has constant coefficient $1$.
nodes.title: Constant term of the Euler products

nodes.summary: For all complex numbers $a$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the infinite product $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$ converges unconditionally to the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol $(a;q)_\infty$: the products of the factors $1 - a q^n$ over finite sets of indices $n$ tend to $(a;q)_\infty$.
nodes.title: Convergence of the infinite q-Pochhammer product

nodes.summary: The Euler product $f_1 = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)$ equals the pentagonal series $\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^j q^{j(3j-1)/2}$ as an integer power series.
nodes.title: Pentagonal series expansion of the first Euler product

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the Euler product $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is this infinite product in the ring of integer power series in $q$, taken in the coefficientwise topology. It is used for $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The Euler products of partition theory

nodes.summary: The infinite q-Pochhammer symbol satisfies $(1;0)_\infty = 0$, because its factor for $n = 0$ is $1 - 1 \cdot 0^0 = 0$ (with the convention $0^0 = 1$).
nodes.title: The q-Pochhammer symbol vanishes at a = 1 and q = 0

nodes.summary: The raw infinite q-Pochhammer product at $a = 2$ and $q = 1$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: The raw q-Pochhammer product at a = 2 and q = 1 equals 1

nodes.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $q$, the raw infinite q-Pochhammer product is the unconditional infinite product $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$, defined for every $q$: when this product does not converge unconditionally (in particular for most $q$ with $|q| \ge 1$), its value is $1$ by convention.
nodes.title: Raw infinite q-Pochhammer product

nodes.summary: For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, $(0;q)_\infty = 1$, since every factor $1 - 0 \cdot q^n$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: The q-Pochhammer symbol with a = 0

nodes.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol is $(a;q)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$, the unconditional infinite product of the factors $1 - a q^n$.
nodes.title: Infinite q-Pochhammer symbol

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
